items.quote: Then the trees said to the vine, ‘Come and be our king.’
items.contrast: The reader must distinguish the trees, who want the king, from the vine, whom they ask to become king, and resolve “our” as referring to the trees.
items.reason: The window establishes that the trees ask the vine to be their king, but “for whose sake” asks about benefit or motive, which is not stated. A bounded rewrite such as “Whose king do the trees ask the vine to become?” would make the keyed relation unique.
